title_candidates: Nativ makes local AI approachable on a Mac
Try an AI model offline on your Mac with Nativ
summary: Nativ gives Apple-silicon Mac users a desktop interface for downloading and chatting with open AI models locally, without an account or subscription.

primary_source.title: Nativ: Run AI models locally on your Mac
primary_source.author: Simon Willison
key_facts: Nativ is a macOS desktop application that runs open AI models locally on Apple-silicon Macs.
The app wraps Apple's MLX ecosystem in a desktop interface with chat and a localhost API server.
Nativ can discover compatible MLX models already stored in a user's Hugging Face cache.
The project requires an M1-or-newer Mac and does not require an account or subscription.
The interface includes streaming chat, Markdown and code rendering, image input, and per-message performance metrics.
The project is open source under the MIT license and is built on MLX-VLM.

prerequisites: An Apple-silicon Mac (M1 or newer) running macOS 26 or later
At least 4 GB of free storage
Internet access for the app and model downloads

steps.instruction: Download the latest Nativ DMG from the official GitHub Releases page, drag Nativ into Applications, and launch it. If macOS blocks it, verify the source instead of bypassing warnings blindly.
Continue through first-launch setup with load-on-demand and confirm the main window opens. Leave remote access disabled for this local test.
Open Models, choose LFM2.5-VL 1.6B (about 3.20 GB), and wait until it is installed and selectable. Avoid larger models for this quick test unless your Mac has ample storage and unified memory.

Start a chat and ask, 'Explain in three bullets why leaves look green.' Confirm a streamed answer and performance metrics appear. Do not use passwords, private documents, or regulated data for this first test.

After the model download finishes, disconnect Wi-Fi and ask, 'Reply with exactly: local test passed.' Confirm it answers offline, then reconnect. Delete the chat and remove the model if you want to reclaim storage.

risk_flags: Local inference reduces cloud exposure but does not make an unreviewed app or model safe for sensitive data.
Model downloads are several gigabytes and larger models may exceed a Mac's practical memory limits.
